title: Rule 30 from a single cell contains every possible block

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Rule 30 from a single cell contains every possible block

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The pattern generated by the rule 30 cellular automaton from a single black cell appears to contain every possible block of cells eventually, so that essentially any possible computation exists somewhere within this single pattern.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. 12: The Principle of Computational Equivalence

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: So far as I can tell, all possible blocks eventually appear, potentially letting the pattern serve as a kind of directory of all possible computations.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 12, “The Principle of Computational Equivalence”; section “The Content of the Principle” (from p. 719), p. 725. Scope: rule 30 elementary cellular automaton started from a single black cell

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch12-06: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.71

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The property is mathematically precise and arbitrarily large finite searches are easy. Existing results do not resolve the infinite quantifier, so a new theorem or counterexample is needed.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For every finite binary word, prove that some row of the single-seed rule 30 spacetime diagram contains it, or find a finite word and prove it never occurs. Enumeration can confirm occurrence only up to finite block length.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The computation-directory interpretation is stronger than block occurrence alone.

No known general occurrence proof or forbidden-block proof settles the claim.

Finite simulation cannot establish the all-blocks quantifier.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 1.0
data adequacy: 0.35
operationalizability: 0.9
analysis feasibility: 0.25
discriminating power: 0.85

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Whether every finite block appears is a precise conjecture about one deterministic pattern, and every fixed length is a finite computation that public software can push well past hand enumeration. Those computations resolve the claim up to a length bound. They do not resolve it for every length, and no proof covering all lengths is available to finish the job.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Generate the rule-30 spacetime diagram from one black cell and record the longest length through which every binary block has appeared. The claim is refuted by any missing block, and confirmed for all lengths only by a proof that every finite block occurs. A search to length n confirms only that restricted statement.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A block could appear extremely far from the center, beyond any practical search, without being absent.

Any finite diagram leaves longer blocks unchecked, so computation confirms a bounded version and cannot by itself prove the universal claim.
